newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo shares tumble after Wall St jolt.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo shares tumble after Wall St jolt.

text.p: Tokyo shares tumbled in early trading on Friday, dragged down by the earlier sharp drop on Wall Street.

The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares briefly fell more than 500 points, or 2.5 percent, to about 19,987 in hectic trade. It was the first time the index had been below the key level of 20,000 in three months.
New York shares fell 1.54 percent on Thursday on a late burst of computerised programme selling after a roller-coaster day.
Stock markets around the globe have been nervous since Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan talked about the possibility of equity markets moving too high.
Speaking a week ago, the head of the U.S. central bank said that "irrational exuberance" could be affecting the markets.
After falling through the important 20,000-point barrier, the Nikkei recovered slightly and stabilised. At 10.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) it was down 427.13 points at 20,074.07, a loss of 2.08 percent.
